- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in the last 3–5 days, model tends to underpredict sharp upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for the next 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.0) and price is trending up, model often overestimates the peak; cap forecast at 1–2% below the 30-day high.
- When model shows steady upward drift with no sentiment spike, true price often reverses or lags — reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 7 days.
- If model forecast is flat or slightly rising while sentiment is neutral, true price often spikes later — add 2–5% upward bias for next 3–5 days.
- If model overestimates early in the 30-day horizon (e.g., first 5–7 days), true price often corrects — apply downward correction of 2–5% for days 8–15.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.2 spikes, model tends to overshoot — apply 1–3% downward correction after each spike.
- If true price exceeds model forecast by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, model is underestimating trend — increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5 days.
- If sentiment is 0.0 for 5+ days and price is flat, true price often reverses — add 1–3% downward bias for next 3–5 days.
- If model forecast is >70% of 30-day true average, it’s likely overconfident — reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 7 days.
- If sentiment is 0.0 and price is trending down, model often underestimates the drop — add 1–3% downward bias for next 5 days.
